definition: Aricept is a brand name for donepezil hydrochloride, a medication that can support thinking and memory by reversibly blocking the enzyme that breaks down acetylcholine, which increases this neurotransmitter’s activity. In the supplied source, it is described as potentially improving neurocognitive function, including in Alzheimer’s disease.

provenance.scope: Source record C2603; pinned source text

reasons: The packet identifies the substance as donepezil hydrochloride but does not support the claim that Aricept is a brand name for it.

The definition adds a general explanatory gloss about supporting thinking and memory; the packet supports neurocognitive-enhancing activity and acetylcholinesterase inhibition, but not that broader phrasing as a term definition in this field.
The packet does not state that Aricept is a brand name for donepezil hydrochloride; it describes donepezil hydrochloride but does not link this to the brand “Aricept.”

The definition claims the medication “can support thinking and memory,” but the packet only describes “neurocognitive-enhancing activity” and does not specifically mention “thinking and memory” in those terms.
